metadata.name: flint_escrow
metadata.description: Flint escrow program — reference Solana adapter for FRS-1 (devnet only)

instructions.name: cancel
docs: Recipient withdraws before funding (`Pending` → `Cancelled`, account
closed, rent back to the recipient).

accounts.name: recipient
docs: The proposer, and the only signer allowed here.

accounts.name: agreement
docs: Closed by Anchor at the end of the instruction: the rent goes back to the
recipient (Section 4.6). Closing also frees the (recipient, id) pair, so
a cancelled agreement can be re-proposed under the same uuid.

accounts.name: escrow_token_account
docs: The (empty) escrow token account, closed too so its rent is not stranded
and the ATA does not block a future re-proposal of the same uuid.
Declared as an `AccountInfo` on purpose: the SPL `close_account` CPI
deactivates the account, and Anchor re-serializing a closed
`Account<'_, TokenAccount>` at exit would fail. Every property this
account must have is therefore checked in the handler instead.
`escrow_address`, owned by the SPL Token program, controlled by this
agreement PDA, denominated in the stored asset, and empty — before it is
closed.

instructions.name: claim_delivery
docs: Recipient claims delivery with a manifest hash and a locator to check it
against (`Funded` -> `DeliveryClaimed`). One claim, and only before
expiry. After this the agreement's expiry has no further effect.

accounts.name: recipient
docs: Must be the agreement's stored recipient (row 1).

instructions.name: create
docs: Recipient proposes an agreement (no state -> `Pending`).

accounts.name: recipient
docs: The proposer: pays for both new accounts and signs the terms.

accounts.name: config
docs: The Config: the protocol minimum and the parameters every agreement
inherits. Present on `create` so an agreement cannot exist below the
minimum, or with a review window outside the allowed set.

accounts.name: asset
docs: The SPL mint the agreement is denominated in (FRS-1 `asset`).

accounts.name: escrow_ata
docs: The escrow token account. Section 4.5: a separate ATA from the PDA, owned
(as an SPL account) by the agreement PDA — which is why only this program
can move what goes into it.

instructions.name: dispute
docs: Payer rejects a claim inside the review window (`DeliveryClaimed` ->
`Disputed`). Moves no money.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Must be the agreement's stored payer (row 1).

accounts.name: config
docs: Read at dispute time so the arbiter's deadline is frozen into the
agreement below. Must be provided because `split_after_arbiter_timeout`
must not re-read a timeout a later admin change could have moved.

instructions.name: fund
docs: First funder deposits the full amount (`Pending` → `Funded`) and becomes
`payerAddress`, permanently.

accounts.name: funder
docs: Becomes `payerAddress`; must own `funder_token_account`.

accounts.name: funder_token_account
docs: The funder's source token account, denominated in the agreement's asset.

accounts.name: escrow_token_account
docs: The agreement's escrow ATA; validated against stored state, never trusted.

instructions.name: init_config
docs: Creates the global Config. Once per program, signed by the upgrade
authority, which becomes the admin.

accounts.name: admin
docs: Must sign, and must be the program's current **upgrade authority** —
enforced below, not merely asserted by this comment.
Binding config control to the upgrade authority means the same key can
already replace the program outright. An admin who is *not* the upgrade
authority could point the treasury at themselves while an uncompromised
authority watched; tying the two makes that an authority compromise
rather than a second, separate trust.

accounts.name: program_data
docs: This program's upgradeable-loader account. Read to obtain the upgrade
authority address. Kept as an `UncheckedAccount` because Anchor has no
typed wrapper for it in the SDK this crate pins (see `read_upgrade_authority`),
so ownership, address and shape are all asserted by hand below.
upgradeable-loader-owned, is the ProgramData PDA of the verified program,
and holds a parseable ProgramData header.

accounts.name: program
docs: The program account itself. Verifying its address against `crate::ID`
stops a caller from passing some *other* upgradeable program whose
authority they control, and its owner must be the upgradeable loader.

instructions.name: refund
docs: Permissionless crank after expiry (`Funded` → `Refunded`); funds go to
the stored payer, never to the caller.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Anyone can crank the refund. This signer only pays the transaction fee —
it is never the beneficiary, which is why the account is not called
"payer": naming it that would invite exactly the confusion row 1 exists
to prevent.

accounts.name: payer_token_account
docs: The stored payer's token account; validated against `payer_address`.

instructions.name: release
docs: The stored payer confirms the condition is met (`Funded` → `Released`).

accounts.name: payer
docs: Must be the agreement's **stored** `payerAddress` (row 1). The recipient
cannot release, and neither can anyone else.

accounts.name: config
docs: The Config, for the treasury the fee is paid to.

accounts.name: recipient_token_account
docs: The recipient's token account for the agreement's asset. Validated
against the stored `recipient_address` — never trusted (row 2).

accounts.name: treasury_token_account
docs: The treasury's token account for this asset, validated against the Config.

instructions.name: release_after_review
docs: Permissionless crank once the review window closes
(`DeliveryClaimed` -> `Released`): silence is a decision.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Anyone may crank this. Like `refund`'s cranker, this signer only pays the
fee and is never a beneficiary — the destination comes from stored state.

accounts.name: config
docs: The Config, for the treasury the fee is paid to.

accounts.name: recipient_token_account
docs: The stored recipient's token account, validated against stored state.

accounts.name: treasury_token_account
docs: The treasury's token account for this asset.

instructions.name: resolve_dispute
docs: Arbiter-only ruling on a dispute. Funds can only ever reach the stored
payer, the stored recipient, or the Config's treasury.

accounts.name: arbiter
docs: Must equal the Config's stored arbiter (row 1).

accounts.name: payer_token_account
docs: The stored payer's token account.

accounts.name: recipient_token_account
docs: The stored recipient's token account.

accounts.name: treasury_token_account
docs: The Config's treasury token account for this asset.

instructions.name: set_config_roles
docs: Admin-only rotation of the treasury, arbiter and arbiter timeout.

accounts.name: admin
docs: Must be the Config's stored admin (row 1).

instructions.name: split_after_arbiter_timeout
docs: Permissionless fixed 50/50 split once the arbiter's window has lapsed
(`Disputed` -> `Split`), so a lost arbiter can never strand the escrow.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Anyone may crank this once the arbiter's window has passed. Payer only in
the sense that the funds reach the stored payer too.

errors.name: RecipientOnly
errors.msg: Only the agreement's recipient can perform this action.

errors.name: PayerOnly
errors.msg: Only the agreement's stored payerAddress can release it.

errors.name: NotPending
errors.msg: This agreement is not pending.

errors.name: NotFunded
errors.msg: This agreement is not funded.

errors.name: NotDisputable
errors.msg: The dispute flag applies only to a funded agreement; pending and settled agreements are not disputable.

errors.name: ExpiryNotInFuture
errors.msg: expiresAt must be strictly in the future when the agreement is created.

errors.name: ExpiredBeforeFunding
errors.msg: This agreement expired before it was funded, so it could never be released.

errors.name: Expired
errors.msg: This agreement has expired — only refund remains valid.

errors.name: NotYetExpired
errors.msg: This agreement has not expired yet; it cannot be refunded.

errors.name: ZeroAmount
errors.msg: The amount must be greater than zero.

errors.name: UnsupportedConditionType
errors.msg: v1 enforces only the manual-confirmation condition; oracle-attested is not implemented.

errors.name: FieldTooLong
errors.msg: A field exceeds its FRS-1 length bound (Section 4.6).

errors.name: AgreementPdaMismatch
errors.msg: The agreement account is not the canonical PDA for its stored id and recipientAddress.

errors.name: EscrowMismatch
errors.msg: The provided token account is not the agreement's stored escrowAddress.

errors.name: AssetMismatch
errors.msg: The token account's mint does not match the agreement's asset.

errors.name: TokenAccountOwnerMismatch
errors.msg: The token account's owner does not match the wallet the agreement requires.

errors.name: FunderTokenAccountMismatch
errors.msg: The funder's token account is not owned by the funding signer.

errors.name: ClaimRecipientOnly
errors.msg: Only the agreement's recipient can claim delivery.

errors.name: ClaimAfterExpiry
errors.msg: Delivery cannot be claimed after the agreement has expired.

errors.name: AlreadyClaimed
errors.msg: This agreement already has a delivery claim; delivery may only be claimed once.

errors.name: EvidenceHashEmpty
errors.msg: The evidence hash must not be all zeros.

errors.name: EvidenceRefEmpty
errors.msg: The evidence reference must not be empty.

errors.name: NotDeliveryClaimed
errors.msg: This agreement is not in delivery-claimed state, so there is no review window.

errors.name: NotDisputed
errors.msg: This agreement is not disputed.

errors.name: AlreadyDisputed
errors.msg: This agreement is already disputed; a dispute cannot be reopened.

errors.name: ReviewWindowOpen
errors.msg: The review window is still open; the payer may still dispute or release.

errors.name: ReviewWindowClosed
errors.msg: The review window has closed, so this claim can no longer be disputed.

errors.name: FeeMathOverflow
errors.msg: A fee or split calculation overflowed, so it was refused rather than approximated.

errors.name: SplitShareOutOfRange
errors.msg: A split share must be between 1 and 9999 basis points.

errors.name: AlreadySettled
errors.msg: This agreement is already settled or finished.

errors.name: BelowMinimumAmount
errors.msg: This amount is below the protocol minimum for an agreement.

errors.name: ReviewWindowNotAllowed
errors.msg: The review window must be one of the allowed values: 6h, 12h, 24h or 48h.

errors.name: ConfigAdminOnly
errors.msg: Only the Config admin can rotate the treasury or arbiter.

errors.name: UpgradeAuthorityProgramMismatch
errors.msg: The program account must be this program.

errors.name: UpgradeAuthorityDataMismatch
errors.msg: The program data account must be this program's ProgramData account.

errors.name: NotUpgradeAuthority
errors.msg: Only the program's upgrade authority can initialize the Config.

errors.name: UpgradeAuthorityRevoked
errors.msg: This program has no upgrade authority, so the Config cannot be initialized.

errors.name: ProgramNotUpgradeable
errors.msg: This program is not upgradeable, so the Config cannot be initialized.

errors.name: ArbiterOnly
errors.msg: Only the Config arbiter can resolve a dispute.

errors.name: ArbiterTimeoutNotReached
errors.msg: The arbiter timeout has not passed, so this dispute cannot be split yet.

errors.name: ArbiterTimeoutZero
errors.msg: The arbiter timeout must be greater than zero.

errors.name: ZeroAddress
errors.msg: This address may not be the all-zero address.

types.name: AgentPolicy
docs: FRS-1 `agentPolicy` — optional, for autonomous payers (Section 6.2).
Evaluated off-chain by the deterministic policy engine (no LLM anywhere in
the pay/no-pay decision path); the program stores it but does not enforce it.

fields.name: spend_cap
docs: FRS-1 `spendCap`, in `asset` base units.

fields.name: allowlist
docs: FRS-1 `allowlist` — permitted recipient addresses.

types.name: AgreementStatus
docs: Lifecycle of an FRS-1 agreement.
The delivery branch is the reason this enum grew: the recipient no longer
merely "confirms" delivery, they *claim* it with evidence, and that claim
opens a review window in which the payer may dispute before money moves.
- `Pending` → `Funded`      : first funder deposits the full `amount`; that
address becomes `payer_address`, permanently.
- `Pending` → `Cancelled`   : recipient only (no payer exists yet).
- `Funded` → `DeliveryClaimed` : recipient claims delivery with evidence,
before `expires_at`. One claim only.
- `Funded` → `Released`     : payer-signed release, from `Funded` or
`DeliveryClaimed`, at any time.
- `Funded` → `Refunded`     : after `expires_at`, permissionless crank, and
only while no claim exists.
- `DeliveryClaimed` → `Released` : `release_after_review`, permissionless once
`claimed_at + review_window_secs` has passed.
- `DeliveryClaimed` → `Disputed` : payer only, inside the review window.
- `Disputed` → `Released` / `Refunded` / `Split` : the arbiter's call, or the
50/50 timeout split once the arbiter is late.
- `Released` / `Refunded` / `Split` / `Cancelled` : terminal.
The claim **detaches the agreement from `expires_at`**: once delivery is
claimed, expiry has no further effect, and `refund` refuses. That is why the
refund path checks the status rather than the clock alone.

types.name: Condition
docs: FRS-1 `condition` — `{ type, description }` (Sections 4.1 / 4.3).

fields.name: condition_type
docs: Serialized as FRS-1's `type` field. The Rust identifier differs only
because `type` is a Rust keyword; the TypeScript side uses `type`.

fields.name: description
docs: Human-readable only — display text, never a verification mechanism.

types.name: ConditionType
docs: The `condition.type` values (Section 4.3).
v1 mechanically enforces exactly one of them. `OracleAttested` is a named
schema value for future use and **is deliberately not implemented in v1** —
no instruction may ever treat it as satisfied, and a free-text
`description` must never gate an on-chain transition.
FRS-1's string form is kebab-case (`"manual-confirmation"` /
`"oracle-attested"`); the app layer owns that mapping (Sections 4.1, 4.3).

types.name: Config
docs: Global protocol configuration, one PDA per program.
Holds the two roles that have to be the *same on every agreement* — the
treasury that receives fees, and the arbiter that resolves disputes — plus
the two parameters the protocol enforces on every agreement (minimum amount,
arbiter timeout). A per-agreement copy of any of these would let an
agreement choose its own arbiter, which is the one authority that must never
be negotiable.
Set once by `init_config`, signed by the upgrade authority. The admin may then
rotate `treasury` and `arbiter`; it may not change the minimum, because the
minimum is what the fee table's floor assumes.

fields.name: admin
docs: May rotate `treasury` and `arbiter`. Initially the upgrade authority.

fields.name: treasury
docs: Receives every fee, in the agreement's own asset.

fields.name: arbiter
docs: The only signer `resolve_dispute` accepts.

fields.name: arbiter_timeout_secs
docs: How long the arbiter has to resolve before `split_after_arbiter_timeout`
becomes available. Read from the Clock sysvar like every other deadline.

fields.name: min_agreement
docs: Minimum agreement size in **whole tokens**; scaled by mint decimals when
compared against a base-unit amount.

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump for the config PDA, so instructions can sign with it.

types.name: DisputeOutcome
docs: How the arbiter resolved a dispute.
`Split` carries the recipient's basis-point share; the payer receives the
remainder. A split share of 0 or 10000 would be a refund or a release wearing
a different name, so both are rejected.

types.name: DisputeReason
docs: Why the payer disputed a delivery claim (`dispute.reason_code` 1..=5).
A code, not free text: it has to be small enough to live on-chain, and a
closed set means the recipient and the arbiter see the same categories.
Borsh serializes this as the variant index (0..=4); the FRS-1 reason codes
1..=5 are that index plus one, mapped by name in the client
(`DISPUTE_REASON_CODES` in `app/lib/frs1-types.ts`). Explicit discriminants
are deliberately *not* used here: Anchor's TypeScript coder writes enum
variants by index, so a `#[borsh(use_discriminant)]` enum would make the
program expect different bytes from what the client sends.

types.name: FlintAgreement
docs: The FRS-1 agreement account (Section 4.1, field-for-field).
Immutability that follows from Section 4.2: once `status` is no longer
`Pending`, the term fields (`amount`, `recipient_address`, `asset`,
`condition`) are never written again — Phase 1 satisfies this by exposing no
instruction that can write them (threat-model row 6).

fields.name: id
docs: FRS-1 `id` — uuid-v4 as 16 raw bytes; also a PDA seed (Section 4.5).

fields.name: payer_address
docs: FRS-1 `payerAddress` — the funding wallet.
`None` while pending. It is set once, atomically with the deposit, to
whoever funds first (open model, first funder wins), and never changes
afterwards. There is therefore no payer authority on a pending
agreement (Section 4.2).

fields.name: recipient_address
docs: FRS-1 `recipientAddress` — set at creation, immutable once funded.

fields.name: title
docs: FRS-1 `title`.

fields.name: amount
docs: FRS-1 `amount` — `u64` base units, always; never a float, anywhere
(Section 4.5). No partial settlement: paid in full or not at all.

fields.name: asset
docs: FRS-1 `asset` — the SPL token mint `Pubkey`, authoritative. A symbol
such as "USDC" is a display-only app-layer lookup (Section 4.5).

fields.name: escrow_address
docs: FRS-1 `escrowAddress` — the **escrow's SPL token account (ATA)**, not
the agreement PDA. The PDA is state/authority; this ATA holds the
tokens, with the PDA (or an escrow-authority PDA derived from it) as its
authority (Section 4.5).

fields.name: memo
docs: FRS-1 `memo`.

fields.name: expires_at
docs: FRS-1 `expiresAt` — compared against the on-chain Clock sysvar only,
never an instruction-supplied timestamp (Section 4.5).

fields.name: status
docs: FRS-1 `status` (Section 4.2).

fields.name: condition
docs: FRS-1 `condition` (Section 4.3).

fields.name: review_window_secs
docs: Review window the creator chose, in seconds. Always one of
[`ALLOWED_REVIEW_WINDOWS`], validated at creation. It starts at
`claimed_at`, not at `expires_at`: the window exists to review a delivery
claim, and there is no claim to review until one exists.

fields.name: claimed_at
docs: When the recipient claimed delivery. `None` until `claim_delivery`.
The whole delivery branch is derived from this field: the review window
closes at `claimed_at + review_window_secs`, and a dispute is only
accepted strictly before that.

fields.name: evidence_hash
docs: SHA-256 of the canonical evidence manifest, committed by the recipient at
claim time.
The *manifest*, not the files: hashing bytes a third party cannot fetch
proves nothing after the fact, whereas a manifest hash can be recomputed
later from the stored manifest and compared, which is exactly what
`/verify` does. All zeros is reserved for "no claim yet" and is rejected
as a claim's hash, so a claim can never look like an empty claim.

fields.name: evidence_ref
docs: Compact locator for the stored manifest, e.g. `flint://e/<id>`.
Bounded by [`MAX_EVIDENCE_REF_LEN`] and required non-empty at claim time:
a hash with no way to reach the bytes it covers would be unverifiable.

fields.name: disputed_at
docs: When the payer disputed a claim. `None` unless the status is `Disputed`.

fields.name: arbiter_deadline
docs: The arbiter's deadline for this dispute, stored at dispute time as
`disputed_at + config.arbiter_timeout_secs`.
Stored rather than recomputed because a live config change must not move
the deadline of an in-flight dispute: shortening it would cut the
arbiter's window, lengthening it would strand the escrow longer.
`split_after_arbiter_timeout` reads this field, never the Config.
`None` unless the status is `Disputed`.

fields.name: dispute_reason
docs: Which reason code the payer gave (1..=5). Meaningful only with `disputed_at`.

fields.name: fee_amount
docs: The protocol fee for this agreement, in base units, **locked at creation**.
Locked rather than recomputed at settlement so that the payer's total cost
is knowable from the agreement the moment it exists, and so a later change
to the fee table cannot retroactively alter what an in-flight agreement
owes. Deducted from the recipient's payout on every path that pays the
recipient (scaled to the recipient's share on a split); never charged on a
refund, which returns the payer's own money.

fields.name: handle
docs: FRS-1 `handle` — optional, display-only in v1 (Flint.ID is roadmap;
nothing resolves this yet).

fields.name: agent_policy
docs: FRS-1 `agentPolicy` — optional (agent flow).

fields.name: receipt_proof
docs: FRS-1 `receiptProof` — the **settlement** (release/refund) transaction
signature, written when settlement happens (Section 4.4). The funding
signature is deliberately not stored; that is an accepted gap because it
is discoverable from the account's on-chain history.
FLAG (raised in Phase 1 — not silently reinterpreted): no instruction
writes this field, and none ever can. A Solana program cannot read its
own transaction's signature, so the signature cannot be produced
on-chain. As implemented, the receipt is the settlement signature the
*client* observes and records, and its validity is established by
recomputing status from this account and checking that transaction
against this program's settlement instruction (Sections 4.4 and 6.2,
threat-model row 7) — which is the property 4.4 actually asks for. The
field is retained so the on-chain account stays a subset of the FRS-1
schema, pending a decision on whether to drop it or replace it with
something the program *can* write (e.g. the settlement slot).
What a receipt proves: that a specific transition occurred, for a
specific amount and asset, authorized by the required signer. What it
does not prove: that the real-world condition was met (Section 4.4).
